observation.visible_scene: Top-down view of a white tabletop. In the upper-left corner sits an open box filled with shiny metallic spheres. To the right is a flat hexagonal lattice (graphene-like sheet) built from metallic spheres linked by short metallic rods. Two hands work on the lower edge of this lattice: the left hand pinches a single free sphere, and the right hand holds a loose rod.
visible_changes: From t=0 to about t=0.6 the scene is nearly static: the left hand keeps the lower sphere fixed while the right hand holds a small detached rod just beside it, making only minor positional adjustments.

Around t=0.7–1.0 the right hand brings the rod into contact with the lower sphere, so a new rod now extends from that sphere toward the lower-right; the right hand then grips the far end of this rod and holds/aligns it for the next ~1 second (t=1.0–2.0), with the left hand still steadying the sphere.

Between t=2.07 and t=2.13 the lower ring abruptly becomes a closed hexagon: additional spheres and rods now form a complete six-membered ring hanging below the original lattice. This completion is not shown as continuous motion (no intermediate placement frames appear), so it reads as an editing cut or an off-camera rapid assembly.

After the ring closes (t=2.13–2.67), the left hand releases the sphere and drifts leftward, eventually resting near the left edge of the original lattice, while the right hand now holds the right-vertex sphere of the new ring, keeping the structure steady.
The box of spheres and the upper part of the lattice remain unchanged and in the same image positions throughout, indicating a stationary camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the remaining spheres/rods of the new hexagon were placed during the jump between t=2.07 and t=2.13.
What happened before t=0 (the lattice was already partly built) and what the builder does after t=2.67.
The exact identity/material of the parts beyond their metallic appearance.
uncertain_details: Whether the t=2.07→2.13 transition is a hard edit cut or merely a very fast assembly not captured by the 15 fps sampling.
The precise frame at which the loose rod first bonds to the lower sphere (somewhere between t=0.67 and t=1.0).
Whether the right hand's small rod in the first frames is the same piece later attached, or a separate component.
